jobs.title: Director of Software Development
jobs.description:
About Karmak

Karmak is a 100% employee-owned software company that has helped keep the commercial transportation industry moving for more than 40 years. Our flagship platform, Karmak Fusion
, powers the parts, service, accounting, and business operations of heavy-duty truck dealerships and transportation companies across North America. Simply put, our customers keep America moving-and we build the technology that helps them do it.

We develop on the Microsoft technology stack, including .NET, SQL Server, and Microsoft Azure
, creating modern, scalable solutions for a mission-critical industry. As employee-owners, we think beyond our individual roles and share responsibility for our company's success. We're looking for leaders who embrace that same ownership mindset and are excited to make a lasting impact.

Position Summary

Remote (US); limited travel (1–2 trips per year)

The Director of Software Development is responsible for the management and daily execution of Karmak's development organization in support of Karmak Fusion. Leading through four development managers spanning application development, QA, and database/reporting teams (a 30+ person engineering organization), this position owns the flow of work between Support, Implementation, Product, DBA, and the development teams; serves as the development-side approval authority on customer patches; and makes go/no-go decisions across a multi-version release train.

The Director is the primary point of escalation into development for the rest of the organization and the VP of Development's operational right hand - a role requiring the technical credibility to challenge a root-cause analysis, the judgment to weigh customer risk on every patch and release decision, and the leadership to run cross-team incident response when a customer-impacting issue crosses team boundaries.

How You'll Operate

This role is built for a high-agency leader. Here is the working relationship you should expect:

You'll get context and priorities from the VP of Development - not task lists. We expect you to identify what will move the needle, commit to outcomes, and run with them. You bring the VP problems with proposed answers, not open questions.
This is not a hands-on coding role, but you haven't stopped being an engineer. You can read C# and SQL, sit in architecture and root-cause reviews and challenge them, and tell a real fix from a symptom patch. Senior engineers respect you because of it.
You own escalations end to end: you move them, you don't track them. When plans change, you re-plan in hours, not weeks, and keep the train moving.
You communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided. Exceptions come with verified data, options, and a recommendation.

What You'll Own In Year One

Success in this role is measured in outcomes, not activity. In your first year, a home run looks like:

Release predictability - Releases and patches across the multi-version release train ship on schedule with fewer defect escapes, and go/no-go discipline holds at every checkpoint - without the VP in the room.
Escalations owned and closed - Escalations from Support, Implementation, and Product get a single accountable owner, are driven to root cause rather than symptom fixes, and are closed with clear communication - they stop bouncing upward.
AI-assisted development adoption - The organization measurably advances on AI-assisted engineering - code analysis, automated review, test automation, and agentic tooling - with honest evaluation of where it multiplies velocity and where it doesn't.
Manager bench strength - The four development managers grow into leaders who plan, prioritize, and make sound calls with less direction - the organization runs well when you step away from it.

Essential Job Functions

Provide technical leadership and direction to the development managers and their teams, assisting with planning, prioritization, technology assessment, professional development, and cross-team coordination
Serve as the development-side approval authority on customer patches, weighing patch-versus-upgrade paths, deployment risk windows, and multi-version complexity; ensure patch decisions protect both the customer and the maintainability of the release line
Own go/no-go decisions at each release checkpoint - integration close, QA greenlight, smoke test, packaging, and staged customer rollout - including the authority to hold or pause a release when quality or customer risk demands it
Serve as the primary point of escalation to development for Support, Implementation, and Product; route issues to the correct team or subject-matter expert, chase them to closure, and keep requestors informed with clear status and next steps
Lead incident response for customer-impacting issues that cross team boundaries; drive to root cause rather than symptom fixes, convene the right people quickly, and communicate resolution paths to stakeholders
Direct the daily product delivery rhythm in partnership with Support, DBA, Installations, and Product, and chair recurring quality reviews with the support organization, converting findings into tracked work items
Keep the VP of Development ahead of surprises: escalate exceptions with verified data, options, and a recommendation; draft customer-facing technical communications for executive review
Manage relationships with external technical consultants and vendors in support of development initiatives
Champion continuous improvement of engineering practice, including branch and merge policy, automated code review, test automation, and AI-assisted development tooling
Manage the personnel activities of the team to include hiring, training, and evaluating employees; lead merit and salary planning through the development managers
Lead the team in change management and effectively apply new process improvements
Embrace self-development, professional growth, and desire for feedback for individual growth
Maintain confidentiality
Be a champion for Karmak and the team

Essential Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.S.) in Computer Science or a related field and a minimum of 10 years of software development experience, including 5+ years leading developers and experience managing managers or an organization of 30+ engineers; or equivalent combination of education and experience
Required: current technical depth on the Microsoft development stack - able to read and reason about .NET code (C#/VB.NET) and Microsoft SQL Server (T-SQL, database design, query performance) well enough to be credible with senior engineers, interrogate a root-cause analysis, and distinguish a real fix from a symptom patch
Strongly preferred: experience running teams that build and operate on Microsoft Azure (PaaS services, cloud architecture) and Azure DevOps for work tracking, pipelines, and release management
Direct experience owning production release and patch decisions for commercial, customer-installed or hosted software, including versioned release trains and customer-impact risk assessment; ERP or other business-critical domain experience strongly preferred
A demonstrated pattern of high-agency ownership: identifying what matters, driving it to done without waiting for direction, and being accountable for outcomes, not just process
Demonstrated pattern of calm incident leadership and cross-functional coordination across support, QA, DBA, and product organizations
Exceptional team leadership skills, including the ability to effectively coach, motivate, and empower team members and develop the judgment of front-line managers
Ability to build and sustain trusted relationships internally and externally, sound judgment in dealing with business issues, and the instinct to communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided
Strong initiative, teamwork, and interpersonal skills; strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting customer-facing technical communications
Capable of working in a growth-oriented environment, with ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent requests, projects, and responsibilities
Hands-on experience adopting AI-assisted development practices (code analysis, automated review, agentic tooling) preferred
Knowledge of the heavy-duty or commercial transportation industry a plus

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. Additional responsibilities may be assigned by Karmak.

The Director of Software Engineering will be a senior leader responsible for leading the design, development, and delivery of innovative, customer-facing financial products and digital services for FMB. Reporting to the CIO, the Director of Software Engineering will own the engineering roadmap and execution, drive technical strategy and scale high-performing engineering teams to support the growth ambitions of FMB. You will oversee the entire software development lifecycle, ensuring that all products are delivered with high quality, exceptional scalability, and robust security, all while aligning with the FMB's overall technology vision.

Essential Duties

Technical Strategy and Execution:

Develop and implement the engineering roadmap in alignment with the CIO?s strategic objectives and the business goals of FMB. Translate product vision into buildable architecture, delivery timelines, and scalable systems.Engineering Leadership and Team Management: Lead, mentor, and scale a diverse team of engineering managers, software developers, data engineers, and automation specialists responsible for building innovative software products. Establish clear roles, expectations, and growth paths for all engineering personnel.

Own the delivery process for all software, overseeing the full development lifecycle from sprint planning to deployment. Implement and enforce engineering best practices, including code quality standards, automated testing strategies, and a rigorous, metrics-driven approach to delivery.Platform and Architectural Oversight: Oversee architectural decisions and technology selection to ensure the scalability, performance, and security of customer-facing systems. With over four decades of expertise, we partner with some of the world’s most influential companies to design and optimize environments that demand precision, scalability, and resilience.

Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.

Position Title:

Power Engineering Director

Position Location

: Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States

Salary

DLB recognizes salary ranges from job boards do not necessarily reflect our pay ranges. In many instances we out-compete those ranges for well-qualified candidates.

Job Summary

DLB is establishing its Power Engineering practice and is seeking a Power Engineering Director to lead and grow this service line from the ground up. This is a practice-building hire — the person who executes the strategic direction, makes the hires, builds technical credibility and positions DLB as a credible provider of utility-scale substation, BESS, microgrid, and grid integration engineering services across utility, renewable energy, data center, and industrial markets.

The Power Engineering Director will serve as the senior technical and operational leader for the practice, partnering with executive leadership to set strategy, develop engineering standards, drive business development, and build the team and capabilities necessary to scale.

The Power Engineering Director operates with a high degree of autonomy, receiving strategic direction from executive leadership. This role is responsible for leading engineering teams, driving strategic initiatives, supporting organizational planning, and developing the people, processes, and technical capabilities necessary to scale the practice. As the practice matures, the Director may also be called upon to support executive leadership in evaluating strategic M&A or partnership opportunities that could accelerate Power Solutions growth, expand delivery capabilities, or add technical depth to the team.

Practice Leadership & Team Management (40%)

Lead, manage, and develop the power engineering team including Lead Engineers, Senior Engineers, and supporting staff across substation, BESS, and grid integration disciplines
Lead strategic planning for the Power Engineering practice in partnership with executive leadership
Provide technical direction, mentorship, and quality oversight across all power engineering projects and deliverables
Serve as the senior technical authority for substation design, BESS/IBR interconnection, protection & control, and grid integration engineering
Establish, implement, and maintain engineering standards, design criteria, QA/QC processes, and quality management systems for the power engineering practice
Oversee engineering deliverables for technical accuracy, constructability, code compliance, and EOR accountability
Partner with DLB executive leadership on practice growth strategy, service line development, and resource planning
Build and maintain DLB's reputation as a qualified power engineering firm with clients, utilities, developers, and industry partners
Develop and execute initiatives that support the long-term growth of the practice, including staffing strategy, technical capabilities, and new service offerings
Identify and develop strategic industry partnerships with specialty engineering firms, electrical contractors, testing companies, and construction partners to support larger and more complex Power Solutions engagements and to extend field execution capability where required.

Client Development & Technical Leadership (25%)

Serve as the senior technical authority and primary engineering point of contact for Power Solutions client engagements, converting ecosystem-sourced opportunities into scoped, contracted work.
Lead technical proposal development, statements of qualification, and RFP responses for power engineering services; provide the engineering credibility that supports DLB’s go-to-market positioning.
Serve as primary client relationship manager for key Power Solutions accounts in the utility, renewable energy, and data center markets once engagements are established.
Activate and expand DLB’s existing client relationships within the Power Solutions scope, identifying engineering service opportunities within accounts the firm already serves.
Support Accenture, Galtra, 2AI-DC, and other ecosystem partners by providing technical input, scoping support, and engineering authority for joint pursuits and shared client opportunities.
Represent DLB at industry conferences, utility meetings, interconnection forums, and technical events as the recognized expert for the Power Solutions practice.
Provide market intelligence to executive leadership on client needs, competitive dynamics, and emerging service opportunities within the utility-scale power engineering space.

Technical Oversight & Project Delivery (25%)

Provide technical oversight and EOR review for power engineering projects across the team, ensuring quality, compliance, and liability management
Review and approve major engineering deliverables, study reports, and stamped documents produced by the team
Manage resource allocation, scheduling, and workload distribution across the power engineering team
Oversee resource forecasting, staffing plans, workload balancing, and utilization across the practice to support sustainable growth
Identify and resolve technical, contractual, and client issues escalated from the project team
Ensure compliance with NESC, NEC, NFPA, ANSI, IEEE, and applicable utility standards across all project deliverables
Support project financial performance including fee management, scope control, and practice profitability
Represent DLB in negotiations and technical discussions with utilities, developers, and AHJs

Reporting (10%)

Report weekly to the Executive Directors and President on practice KPIs, revenue pipeline, headcount status, and financial performance against growth targets; maintain a standing executive dashboard for the Power Engineering practice.
Own practice P&L reporting and budget management; track and communicate variances, utilization rates, and margin performance on a regular cadence.
Maintain and report on the business development pipeline for the Power Engineering practice; provide regular pipeline updates to executive leadership including qualified opportunities, proposal activity, and win/loss trends.
Own the practice hiring roadmap; report regularly on recruiting progress, open requisitions, offer activity, and team capacity relative to project demand.
Monitor and communicate engineering quality, delivery performance, and client satisfaction metrics across the practice portfolio; escalate risks and issues to executive leadership with recommended corrective actions.

Technology, Digital Tools & AI-Enabled Efficiency

Identify opportunities and leverage technology, digital platforms, and AI-enabled tools to enhance efficiency through workflow automation, reduced manual effort, and improved accuracy in forecasting, documentation, reporting, and quality processes.
Support adoption of emerging technologies -- including advanced analytics, data visualization tools, and digital construction management platforms -- to strengthen readiness, quality assurance, and project controls.
Collaborate with internal teams to ensure technology solutions align with DLB standards for data security, privacy, and operational integrity.
Support a culture that embraces innovation, continuous improvement, and the strategic use of technology to optimize performance and scalability.

Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned

Knowledge of organizational objectives and how they relate to company policies  
Demonstrated ability to lead organizational initiatives, develop engineering standards, and influence strategic business decisions
Experience leading practice growth through hiring, mentoring, client development, and operational planning
Deep knowledge of utility-scale power engineering including substation design (AIS/GIS), BESS/IBR interconnection, protection & control, and grid integration across medium- and high-voltage systems
Demonstrated experience managing engineering teams and leading multi-disciplinary power systems projects from concept through commissioning
Strong business development skills including client relationship management, proposal leadership, and engineering services market development
Strong working knowledge of NESC, NEC, NFPA, ANSI, IEEE (1547, 2800, 80, 1584, 519), and utility interconnection standards
Knowledge of power systems analysis tools (ETAP, SKM, ASPEN) and working familiarity with EMT/transient simulation methodologies
Proven track record managing engineering practice P&L, team performance, and multi-project portfolios
Skilled at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management
Highly organized with strong attention to detail, able to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and meet tight deadlines under pressure

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager – Incident Response
jobs.description:
Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll lead high-impact incident response work in a complex cloud environment and help shape how Atlassian responds to security events at scale. You’ll lead or coordinate complex security incidents, bringing structure, urgency, and sound judgment under pressure. You’ll partner with Detection, Security Engineering, Product Security, Legal, Crisis Communications, Support, and senior leadership to drive investigation, containment, recovery, and follow-through. You’ll directly manage a team of 5-8 in the US region.

You’ll coach incident responders and senior practitioners, raising the quality of investigations, handoffs, decision-making, and executive communication. You’ll improve the incident response system through playbooks, metrics, exercises, post-incident reviews, and better tooling. A key part of the role will be driving the adoption of investigative AI tools and automation that help analysts triage faster, surface relevant signals, reduce toil, and improve consistency without compromising judgment or security rigor.

You’ll also support regulated and high-trust environments, including work that requires a strong understanding of formal incident handling, reporting expectations, and documented operating procedures.

What You’ll Bring

On day one, we’ll expect you to bring a strong mix of incident leadership, operational maturity, and people leadership. You’ll have experience directly leading complex, multi-stakeholder security incidents in a SaaS, cloud, or enterprise environment, along with demonstrated success managing and developing senior security engineers, incident responders, and/or technical leads.

You’ll have strong executive communication skills, including the ability to translate incomplete technical information into clear decisions, risks, and next steps. You’ll have experience improving incident response programs through metrics, retrospectives, process design, readiness exercises, and cross-team influence, as well as hands-on familiarity with investigation workflows, detection and response tooling, log analysis, and operational coordination across globally distributed teams.

You should have experience deploying investigative AI tools and automation in security operations or incident response environments, including using automation to reduce analyst toil, improve triage quality, accelerate investigations, enrich cases, retrieve relevant knowledge, summarize findings, or orchestrate response workflows. You’ll also bring strong systems thinking: the ability to connect incidents to broader improvements in telemetry, detection logic, escalation paths, tooling, and operating models, together with calm, structured decision-making in ambiguous, high-pressure situations.

What Will Set You Apart

Experience serving as an incident commander or major incident manager for high-severity cyber incidents will help you stand out, as will experience supporting regulated environments or formal incident reporting obligations, including government or FedRAMP-adjacent contexts. We’ll value experience building or scaling follow-the-sun incident response models across regions and introducing AI-assisted investigation workflows, case enrichment, knowledge retrieval, summarization, or orchestration capabilities in security operations.

Strong understanding of how to use operational metrics, quality signals, and error patterns to guide program investments is valuable, as is experience speaking externally, representing security programs, or contributing to broader security community practices.

Our team culture

The Incident Response team values calm execution, clear communication, and continuous learning. We are collaborative, direct, and low-ego during incidents, and we expect leaders to care about both outcomes and the health of the people doing the work. We use blameless review, measurable improvement, and thoughtful automation to get better over time. We want leaders who can set a high bar while creating trust, psychological safety, and accountability across regions and functions.

Why this role matters

This is a rare opportunity to lead one of the most important security functions in a global software company. You’ll influence how Atlassian handles major incidents, matures its response capabilities, and invests in the future of security operations. You’ll work on meaningful problems at the intersection of incident command, operations, engineering, and trust, help define how investigative AI and automation can responsibly improve security response at scale, and partner with senior security and business leaders while building durable systems, stronger responders, and better outcomes for customers.

Compensation

At Atlassian, we strive to design equitable, explainable, and competitive compensation programs. We follow consistent hiring practices and account for each candidate's skills, knowledge, and experience when setting base pay within the range.

Please visit go.atlassian.com/payzones for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

This role may also be eligible for benefits, bonuses, commissions, and equity.

We believe that the unique contributions of all Atlassians create our success. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Position Summary

The Director of Engineering is a hands-on working leader
responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance, repair, and overall condition of Chaminade Resort & Spa’s physical property. This position requires a strong technical background and an individual who is comfortable working alongside the Engineering team—not simply directing from an office.

The Director of Engineering will lead by example, personally assisting with troubleshooting, repairs, preventative maintenance, inspections, projects, and emergency response. This position is responsible for ensuring that guest rooms, public spaces, back-of-house areas, mechanical systems, grounds, recreational facilities, and resort infrastructure are maintained to the highest standards of safety, functionality, and appearance.

The ideal candidate is a working engineer and strong leader
who can diagnose problems, pick up a tool when needed, teach the team, prioritize work, and hold themselves and others accountable for maintaining a premier resort property.

Hands-On Engineering & Maintenance

Serve as an active, working member of the Engineering team and regularly perform maintenance and repair work throughout the property.
Personally troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical, HVAC, mechanical, carpentry, appliance, and general building maintenance issues.
Respond directly to guest room and public area maintenance calls when needed.
Perform preventative maintenance inspections and repairs throughout the resort.
Conduct daily property walks to identify maintenance, safety, cleanliness, and appearance concerns.
Inspect guest rooms, meeting spaces, public areas, back-of-house areas, pools, spa facilities, recreational areas, and grounds.
Assist Engineering team members with complex repairs and technical issues.
Train team members through hands-on demonstration and coaching.
Maintain tools, equipment, mechanical rooms, workshops, and Engineering storage areas in a clean, organized, and professional condition.
Be willing and able to work alongside the team during periods of high workload, staffing shortages, emergencies, or major projects.
Respond to emergency maintenance situations and facility-related guest concerns quickly and professionally.

Building Systems & Equipment

Maintain and troubleshoot HVAC systems, electrical systems, plumbing, pumps, water systems, boilers, appliances, lighting, mechanical equipment, and other property systems.
Oversee and personally participate in preventative maintenance programs.
Monitor building automation and energy management systems.
Maintain pools, spas, water features, and related mechanical and chemical systems in accordance with applicable requirements.
Ensure fire/life safety systems and emergency equipment are properly maintained and inspected.
Maintain accurate records of equipment, repairs, inspections, warranties, and preventative maintenance.

Lead the Engineering team through a hands-on management approach.
Set the standard for work quality, urgency, professionalism, and guest service.
Work alongside Engineering associates and provide coaching and technical guidance in real time.
Train team members on proper repair techniques, preventative maintenance, safety procedures, and equipment operation.
Schedule and assign daily work based on occupancy, guest needs, property priorities, and staffing levels.
Monitor completion and quality of work orders.
Hold team members accountable for performance, attendance, productivity, safety, and department standards.
Create a culture where the Engineering team takes pride in the appearance and condition of the resort.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, performance management, and development of Engineering associates.

Develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive preventative maintenance program.
Establish recurring inspection and maintenance schedules for guest rooms, equipment, mechanical systems, and facilities.
Track completion of preventative maintenance and identify recurring issues.
Analyze equipment failures and determine root causes to reduce repeat repairs.
Proactively identify aging equipment and recommend replacement or improvement.
Ensure guest rooms and facilities are returned to excellent condition following repairs.

Be actively involved in renovation and construction projects from planning through completion.
Perform hands-on work when appropriate and coordinate Engineering labor to support projects.
Manage contractors and vendors while ensuring work meets property standards.
Inspect completed work and identify deficiencies requiring correction.
Minimize disruption to guests and hotel operations during projects.

Support resort sustainability and environmental initiatives.

We, at Leggett & Platt Inc., are searching for a Director of Engineering within our engineering team to help support our bedding business. Did you know we have been revolutionizing the sleep industry since 1883? That’s right! In fact, we hold the original patent on a spiral steel coil bed spring, filed way back in 1885. Since then, we have been an industry leader in guaranteeing you get the best sleep possible. If you join our team, your work will ensure people across the world have a little more comfort in their lives.

As a Director of Engineering you will have the opportunity to serve as a player-coach who improves equipment performance, builds engineering capability, establishes practical engineering standards, strengthens project discipline, and creates a more effective bridge between Product Development, Quality, Manufacturing, internal engineering teams, key branches, and external or affiliated engineering partners. . Your contributions will have a direct impact on the business by strengthening engineering and manufacturing execution across business unit operations. The role provides leadership for capital planning, machinery development, industrial and process engineering, controls, automation, electrical engineering, technical documentation, and the transition of new products into stable manufacturing performance. . The team you will be working with is collaborative and innovative, and values challenging work and diversity of thought.

This role offers a relocation opportunity if not local to Carthage, MO.

So, what will you be doing as a Director of Engineering?

Engineering Leadership & Capability Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a multi-disciplinary engineering organization spanning machinery development, industrial and process engineering, controls, automation, electrical engineering, and drafting.
Establish and reinforce clear engineering standards, documentation expectations, design rigor, decision rights, and project discipline across all supported sites.

New Product Introduction & Manufacturing Readiness

Own the transition from new product development to stable, capable, and mature manufacturing performance.
This includes planning and preparing for manufacturing through the product development stage gate process from early concept through sample runs, beta runs, PPAP, validation, launch, ramp-up, and post-launch stabilization.
Ensure Design for Manufacturability (DFM), process capability, control plans, equipment readiness, tooling, documentation, training, and service/support requirements are addressed early enough to prevent launch friction.

Project & Program Management

Provide disciplined project leadership with respect to timing, resources, cost, scope, risk, and cross-functional accountability for engineering and manufacturing readiness initiatives.
Establish project plans with visible milestones, owners, constraints, decision points, and escalation paths so that launch and capital work can be managed proactively rather than reactively.
Maintain clear communication around project status, tradeoffs, risks, cost impacts, and expected business outcomes.

Manufacturing Engagement & Technical Leadership

Maintain regular presence in manufacturing operations to understand equipment, process flow, quality, reliability, and operator challenges firsthand.
Provide hands-on technical leadership on high-impact equipment, process, tooling, automation, and control issues where experience and judgment are critical.
Partner with manufacturing and maintenance leaders to improve equipment reliability, maintainability, operational stability, and responsiveness to production needs.
Support and sustain Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) strategies that reduce downtime, extend asset life, and improve overall equipment effectiveness.

Accelerating Competitive Excellence, Automation and Process Improvement

Drive continuous improvement using Lean manufacturing principles, value stream thinking, level loading, practical material flow improvements, and structured problem solving.
Apply SPC, process capability analysis, root-cause analysis, and disciplined experimentation to improve quality, consistency, and predictability.
Lead automation and manufacturing technology initiatives that deliver measurable operational, quality, safety, and financial benefit.
Use ACE principles to make continuous improvement part of daily work, reinforce common language and methodology, and build capability through real business problems.

Capital Projects & Asset Leadership

Lead and review major capital projects, ensuring strong project rigor, schedule discipline, resource planning, cost control, and return on investment.
Support capital planning and prioritization, including project justification, execution oversight, commissioning, and post-implementation review.
Ensure engineering standards, specifications, spare parts planning, and technical documentation support long-term asset performance, maintainability, safety, and lifecycle cost.

To Be Successful In This Role, You’ll Need

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Industrial, Electrical, Manufacturing, or related discipline).
12-15+ years of progressive engineering experience in a manufacturing environment, including meaningful leadership responsibility.
Demonstrated success leading engineering teams, machinery development, automation, manufacturing process improvement, and launch readiness activities.
Strong project/program management capability with demonstrated ownership of schedules, resources, cost, risk management, cross-functional alignment, and stakeholder communication.
Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, value stream mapping, TPM, capital project execution, SPC, Six Sigma, PFMEA, PPAP, and structured root-cause problem solving.
Ability to work effectively across operations, quality, product development, engineering partners, suppliers, and multiple manufacturing sites.
Proven ability to balance hands-on technical involvement with leadership, coaching, organizational development, and disciplined execution.

Things We Consider a Plus

Additional education and/or certifications.

What To Do Next

Now that you’ve had a chance to learn more about us, what are you waiting for! Apply today and allow us the opportunity to learn more about you and the value you can bring to our team. Once you apply, be sure to create a profile, and sign up for job alerts, so you can be the first to know when new opportunities become available.

Our Values

Our values speak to our shared beliefs, and describe how we approach working together.

Put People First reflects our commitment to safety and care of each other, learning and development, and creating an inclusive environment of mutual respect, empathy and belonging.
Do the Right Thing focuses us on acting with honesty and integrity, delivering the results the right way, taking pride in our work, and speaking the truth – good or bad.
Do Great Work…Together occurs when we engage without hierarchy, collaborate as a team, embrace challenges, and work for the good of all of us.
Take Ownership and Raise the Bar demonstrates our responsibility to add value and make a difference, challenge the status quo and biases to make things better, foster innovative and creative solutions to drive impact, and explore new perspectives and embrace change.

About The Business

Quilter plc is a leading wealth management business, helping to enable brighter financial futures for every generation. Quilter oversees £141.9 billion in customer investments (as of March 2026). It has an adviser and customer offering spanning financial advice, investment platforms, multi-asset investment solutions, and discretionary fund management. The business is comprised of two segments: Affluent and High Net Worth.

Affluent encompasses the financial planning business, Quilter Financial Planning, the Quilter Investment Platform and Quilter Investors, the multi-asset investment solutions business. High Net Worth includes the discretionary fund management business, Quilter Cheviot, together with Quilter Cheviot Financial Planning – offering a highly personalised service to private clients, charities, trustees, and professional partners. Quilter Cheviot has presence throughout the UK, Ireland and Channel Islands.

At Quilter we never stand still. Our foundations are rooted in our extraordinary expertise, which is trusted by hundreds of thousands of customers, but we have great ambitions to stay one step ahead and make an even greater difference to the people and communities we serve, including our colleagues.

Our business is transforming, continually modernising, and becoming even more customer centric. So, if you want to be bold in the pursuit of your ambitions, bring new ideas, and challenge and evolve what we do, it’s the perfect time to join us!

About The Role

As the Head of Engineering, you will be the enterprise owner of the engineering capability. The role is accountable for ensuring that the organisation’s technology platforms, regardless of buy or built are delivered to a consistently high engineering standard that is defined and governed within the engineering practice.

You will report to the CTDO and act as a senior technology partner to business, product, change, architecture, infrastructure, information security, data, operations and third-party delivery partners. The role requires strong functional and technical leadership, and stakeholder influence across a regulated environment

The role is required to build the quality engineering practice, DevSecOps enablement, engineering standards, tooling, career frameworks and the safe adoption of AI-assisted software delivery.

Key responsibilities

Define and execute the engineering strategy aligned to business, technology and product priorities
Establish the engineering operating model, including team struc#
tures, accountabilities, ways of working and decision rights aligned with the broader ways of working for Quilter
Provide technical leadership across the engineering teams and ensure appropriate engineering governance that is light touch and ensures execution at pace is not compromised.
Maintain awareness of emerging technology and engineering trends and translate to meaningful and purposeful conversations and initiatives that drive business value
Build and lead a high-performing Engineering organisation, creating a culture of technical excellence, accountability, innovation, continuous improvement and customer focus.
Define and evolve Quilter's engineering strategy, ensuring engineering investments, capabilities and practices support business priorities, customer outcomes and long-term technology goals.
Establish and continuously improve engineering standards covering software design, coding, quality engineering, integration, deployment and production stability. Lead the evolution of engineering enablement capabilities, including platform engineering, developer tooling, automation and self-service engineering services, reducing friction and improving the effectiveness of software delivery teams.
Continuously improve developer experience (DevEx) by providing engineers with the tools, environments, processes and support required to build, test, deploy and operate software efficiently and safely. Use DORA or complimentary engineering metrics to understand delivery performance and engineering productivity.
Establish and evolve the platform engineering capability that enables engineering teams to build, test, deploy and operate software through self service or SDK (self development kit)
Partner with Enterprise and Solution Architecture to ensure engineering decisions support the organisation’s target architecture by attending ARB and ensuring that architectural decisions are cascaded to the engineering communities. Promote modular, API and event driven architectures.
Drive the evolution of Quality Engineering, embedding quality throughout the software development lifecycle through automation, performance engineering, test data management, production feedback loops and shared accountability for quality outcomes. Establish quality gates and automated controls throughout the software development life cycle.
Define and lead the organisation’s strategy for AI assisted software engineering. Enable engineers to safely use AI coding assistants. Establish appropriate governance for AI generated code.
Develop engineering practices that move teams from AI coding assistants towards effective human + AI workflows
Drive modern software engineering practices by owning and continuously enhance DevSecOps capabilities, including CI/CD, automated testing, infrastructure as a code, API first development and secure software development.
Build a culture of small, frequent, safe releases rather than large, high risk release deployments
Embed security throughout the engineering lifecycle, implement automated security controls within CI/CD pipelines including code scanning and vulnerability management. Establish secure coding practices and engineering security standards. Work with the cyber security team to implement security policies and practices.
Establish clear engineering accountability with you build it you run concept
Balance internal and external delivery capabilities, ensuring the organisation has the right mix of skills, capacity, succession planning and commercial oversight to meet evolving business demand.
Lead the engineering profession across Quilter, including engineering communities, career frameworks, capability development, technical leadership, coaching and succession planning.
Manage technology, delivery and operational risks through proportionate governance, assurance and evidence-based decision-making, enabling teams to deliver at pace while maintaining appropriate controls.
Act as a senior technology leader and trusted adviser, translating complex engineering challenges into clear business implications, options and recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Lead organisational and engineering change in a pragmatic and outcome-focused manner, helping teams adopt modern engineering practices and deliver fast, secure and sustainable customer and business outcomes.
Mature the engineering function by building out the engineering skill sets aligned to the technology strategy and strategic skill sets required to execute on the organisation’s ambition
Provide engineering oversight of strategic technology partners and vendors that provide outsourced engineering capabilities
Create a culture of innovation and curiosity within the engineering community by driving hackathons, system thinking and engineering mindset

About You

You are an experienced engineering leader with a track record of building high-performing teams and delivering technology at scale. Comfortable operating in complex, regulated environments, you combine strong technical expertise with commercial awareness and the ability to influence at senior levels.

You will bring:

Experience leading large engineering organisations through growth, transformation and change.
Experience introducing AI-assisted engineering practices, including coding assistants, automation and AI-enabled software delivery.
Strong understanding of quality engineering, test automation and building quality into the software lifecycle.
A proven ability to build high-performing teams and cultures focused on excellence, accountability and continuous improvement.
Strong experience aligning engineering outcomes to business strategy, customer needs and organisational priorities.
Deep knowledge of modern engineering practices, including Agile, DevSecOps, cloud technologies, automation, CI/CD and secure software development.
Experience improving developer productivity through platform engineering, developer tooling and self-service capabilities.
A passion for Developer Experience (DevEx) and creating environments where engineers can thrive.
Commercially focused decision-making, balancing innovation, delivery, risk, technical debt and long-term sustainability.
Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and communicate effectively at Executive level.
The ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business outcomes and recommendations.
A collaborative leadership style with a passion for coaching, developing talent and building future capability.
Experience leading organisational change and embedding modern ways of working.
Experience with Microsoft technologies, including Azure, GitHub, Azure DevOps, Power Platform and Dynamics 365, would be advantageous.

Inclusion & Diversity

We value diversity and strive to promote inclusivity in all aspects of our culture. We believe in equal opportunities for all, ensuring that no applicant encounters less favourable treatment based on anything but their skills, qualifications, experience, and potential. We celebrate the unique contributions of a diverse workforce and create a respectful, nurturing environment where every colleague can thrive.

Values

Do the right thing:
We act with integrity and are proudly committed to going above and beyond in service of our clients and the support we provide our communities.

Always curious:
We continuously seek new ideas and knowledge so we’re one step ahead of our clients’ needs. We look for inspiration everywhere and encourage experimentation, recognising that this is how we create brilliant solutions for brighter futures.

Embrace challenge:
We aim high to transform our potential into meaningful outcomes. With ambition as our driving force and a steadfast commitment to growth, we succeed for the good of every generation.

Stronger together:
Combining our diverse talents, we accomplish more collectively than we ever could do alone. We speak openly, actively listen, and support each other, and constructively challenge and embrace new ideas. We seek empowerment and demonstrate ownership and trust, with the confidence to make impactful decisions.

182 hours (26 days)

Quilter Incentive Scheme:
All employees are eligible to participate in incentive scheme, to incentivise business performance and their contribution.

Single cover as standard with options to increase cover to include your partner or children.

4x your salary.

75% of salary, less state benefits, payable after 26 weeks of absence.

About Karmak

Karmak is a 100% employee-owned software company that has helped keep the commercial transportation industry moving for more than 40 years. Our flagship platform, Karmak Fusion
, powers the parts, service, accounting, and business operations of heavy-duty truck dealerships and transportation companies across North America. Simply put, our customers keep America moving-and we build the technology that helps them do it.

We develop on the Microsoft technology stack, including .NET, SQL Server, and Microsoft Azure
, creating modern, scalable solutions for a mission-critical industry. As employee-owners, we think beyond our individual roles and share responsibility for our company's success. We're looking for leaders who embrace that same ownership mindset and are excited to make a lasting impact.

Position Summary

Remote (US); limited travel (1–2 trips per year)

The Director of Software Development is responsible for the management and daily execution of Karmak's development organization in support of Karmak Fusion. Leading through four development managers spanning application development, QA, and database/reporting teams (a 30+ person engineering organization), this position owns the flow of work between Support, Implementation, Product, DBA, and the development teams; serves as the development-side approval authority on customer patches; and makes go/no-go decisions across a multi-version release train.

The Director is the primary point of escalation into development for the rest of the organization and the VP of Development's operational right hand - a role requiring the technical credibility to challenge a root-cause analysis, the judgment to weigh customer risk on every patch and release decision, and the leadership to run cross-team incident response when a customer-impacting issue crosses team boundaries.

How You'll Operate

This role is built for a high-agency leader. Here is the working relationship you should expect:

You'll get context and priorities from the VP of Development - not task lists. We expect you to identify what will move the needle, commit to outcomes, and run with them. You bring the VP problems with proposed answers, not open questions.
This is not a hands-on coding role, but you haven't stopped being an engineer. You can read C# and SQL, sit in architecture and root-cause reviews and challenge them, and tell a real fix from a symptom patch. Senior engineers respect you because of it.
You own escalations end to end: you move them, you don't track them. When plans change, you re-plan in hours, not weeks, and keep the train moving.
You communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided. Exceptions come with verified data, options, and a recommendation.

What You'll Own In Year One

Success in this role is measured in outcomes, not activity. In your first year, a home run looks like:

Release predictability - Releases and patches across the multi-version release train ship on schedule with fewer defect escapes, and go/no-go discipline holds at every checkpoint - without the VP in the room.
Escalations owned and closed - Escalations from Support, Implementation, and Product get a single accountable owner, are driven to root cause rather than symptom fixes, and are closed with clear communication - they stop bouncing upward.
AI-assisted development adoption - The organization measurably advances on AI-assisted engineering - code analysis, automated review, test automation, and agentic tooling - with honest evaluation of where it multiplies velocity and where it doesn't.
Manager bench strength - The four development managers grow into leaders who plan, prioritize, and make sound calls with less direction - the organization runs well when you step away from it.

Essential Job Functions

Provide technical leadership and direction to the development managers and their teams, assisting with planning, prioritization, technology assessment, professional development, and cross-team coordination
Serve as the development-side approval authority on customer patches, weighing patch-versus-upgrade paths, deployment risk windows, and multi-version complexity; ensure patch decisions protect both the customer and the maintainability of the release line
Own go/no-go decisions at each release checkpoint - integration close, QA greenlight, smoke test, packaging, and staged customer rollout - including the authority to hold or pause a release when quality or customer risk demands it
Serve as the primary point of escalation to development for Support, Implementation, and Product; route issues to the correct team or subject-matter expert, chase them to closure, and keep requestors informed with clear status and next steps
Lead incident response for customer-impacting issues that cross team boundaries; drive to root cause rather than symptom fixes, convene the right people quickly, and communicate resolution paths to stakeholders
Direct the daily product delivery rhythm in partnership with Support, DBA, Installations, and Product, and chair recurring quality reviews with the support organization, converting findings into tracked work items
Keep the VP of Development ahead of surprises: escalate exceptions with verified data, options, and a recommendation; draft customer-facing technical communications for executive review
Manage relationships with external technical consultants and vendors in support of development initiatives
Champion continuous improvement of engineering practice, including branch and merge policy, automated code review, test automation, and AI-assisted development tooling
Manage the personnel activities of the team to include hiring, training, and evaluating employees; lead merit and salary planning through the development managers
Lead the team in change management and effectively apply new process improvements
Embrace self-development, professional growth, and desire for feedback for individual growth
Maintain confidentiality
Be a champion for Karmak and the team

Essential Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.S.) in Computer Science or a related field and a minimum of 10 years of software development experience, including 5+ years leading developers and experience managing managers or an organization of 30+ engineers; or equivalent combination of education and experience
Required: current technical depth on the Microsoft development stack - able to read and reason about .NET code (C#/VB.NET) and Microsoft SQL Server (T-SQL, database design, query performance) well enough to be credible with senior engineers, interrogate a root-cause analysis, and distinguish a real fix from a symptom patch
Strongly preferred: experience running teams that build and operate on Microsoft Azure (PaaS services, cloud architecture) and Azure DevOps for work tracking, pipelines, and release management
Direct experience owning production release and patch decisions for commercial, customer-installed or hosted software, including versioned release trains and customer-impact risk assessment; ERP or other business-critical domain experience strongly preferred
A demonstrated pattern of high-agency ownership: identifying what matters, driving it to done without waiting for direction, and being accountable for outcomes, not just process
Demonstrated pattern of calm incident leadership and cross-functional coordination across support, QA, DBA, and product organizations
Exceptional team leadership skills, including the ability to effectively coach, motivate, and empower team members and develop the judgment of front-line managers
Ability to build and sustain trusted relationships internally and externally, sound judgment in dealing with business issues, and the instinct to communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided
Strong initiative, teamwork, and interpersonal skills; strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting customer-facing technical communications
Capable of working in a growth-oriented environment, with ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent requests, projects, and responsibilities
Hands-on experience adopting AI-assisted development practices (code analysis, automated review, agentic tooling) preferred
Knowledge of the heavy-duty or commercial transportation industry a plus

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. Additional responsibilities may be assigned by Karmak.

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll lead high-impact incident response work in a complex cloud environment and help shape how Atlassian responds to security events at scale. You’ll lead or coordinate complex security incidents, bringing structure, urgency, and sound judgment under pressure. You’ll partner with Detection, Security Engineering, Product Security, Legal, Crisis Communications, Support, and senior leadership to drive investigation, containment, recovery, and follow-through. You’ll directly manage a team of 5-8 in the US region.

You’ll coach incident responders and senior practitioners, raising the quality of investigations, handoffs, decision-making, and executive communication. You’ll improve the incident response system through playbooks, metrics, exercises, post-incident reviews, and better tooling. A key part of the role will be driving the adoption of investigative AI tools and automation that help analysts triage faster, surface relevant signals, reduce toil, and improve consistency without compromising judgment or security rigor.

You’ll also support regulated and high-trust environments, including work that requires a strong understanding of formal incident handling, reporting expectations, and documented operating procedures.

What You’ll Bring

On day one, we’ll expect you to bring a strong mix of incident leadership, operational maturity, and people leadership. You’ll have experience directly leading complex, multi-stakeholder security incidents in a SaaS, cloud, or enterprise environment, along with demonstrated success managing and developing senior security engineers, incident responders, and/or technical leads.

You’ll have strong executive communication skills, including the ability to translate incomplete technical information into clear decisions, risks, and next steps. You’ll have experience improving incident response programs through metrics, retrospectives, process design, readiness exercises, and cross-team influence, as well as hands-on familiarity with investigation workflows, detection and response tooling, log analysis, and operational coordination across globally distributed teams.

You should have experience deploying investigative AI tools and automation in security operations or incident response environments, including using automation to reduce analyst toil, improve triage quality, accelerate investigations, enrich cases, retrieve relevant knowledge, summarize findings, or orchestrate response workflows. You’ll also bring strong systems thinking: the ability to connect incidents to broader improvements in telemetry, detection logic, escalation paths, tooling, and operating models, together with calm, structured decision-making in ambiguous, high-pressure situations.

What Will Set You Apart

Experience serving as an incident commander or major incident manager for high-severity cyber incidents will help you stand out, as will experience supporting regulated environments or formal incident reporting obligations, including government or FedRAMP-adjacent contexts. We’ll value experience building or scaling follow-the-sun incident response models across regions and introducing AI-assisted investigation workflows, case enrichment, knowledge retrieval, summarization, or orchestration capabilities in security operations.

Strong understanding of how to use operational metrics, quality signals, and error patterns to guide program investments is valuable, as is experience speaking externally, representing security programs, or contributing to broader security community practices.

Our team culture

The Incident Response team values calm execution, clear communication, and continuous learning. We are collaborative, direct, and low-ego during incidents, and we expect leaders to care about both outcomes and the health of the people doing the work. We use blameless review, measurable improvement, and thoughtful automation to get better over time. We want leaders who can set a high bar while creating trust, psychological safety, and accountability across regions and functions.

Why this role matters

This is a rare opportunity to lead one of the most important security functions in a global software company. You’ll influence how Atlassian handles major incidents, matures its response capabilities, and invests in the future of security operations. You’ll work on meaningful problems at the intersection of incident command, operations, engineering, and trust, help define how investigative AI and automation can responsibly improve security response at scale, and partner with senior security and business leaders while building durable systems, stronger responders, and better outcomes for customers.

who can diagnose problems, pick up a tool when needed, teach the team, prioritize work, and hold themselves and others accountable for maintaining a premier resort property.

Serve as an active, working member of the Engineering team and regularly perform maintenance and repair work throughout the property.

Respond directly to guest room and public area maintenance calls when needed.
Perform preventative maintenance inspections and repairs throughout the resort.
Conduct daily property walks to identify maintenance, safety, cleanliness, and appearance concerns.
Inspect guest rooms, meeting spaces, public areas, back-of-house areas, pools, spa facilities, recreational areas, and grounds.
Assist Engineering team members with complex repairs and technical issues.
Train team members through hands-on demonstration and coaching.

Train team members on proper repair techniques, preventative maintenance, safety procedures, and equipment operation.
Schedule and assign daily work based on occupancy, guest needs, property priorities, and staffing levels.
Monitor completion and quality of work orders.
Hold team members accountable for performance, attendance, productivity, safety, and department standards.
Create a culture where the Engineering team takes pride in the appearance and condition of the resort.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, performance management, and development of Engineering associates.

About The Role

As the Head of Engineering, you will be the enterprise owner of the engineering capability. The role is accountable for ensuring that the organisation’s technology platforms, regardless of buy or built are delivered to a consistently high engineering standard that is defined and governed within the engineering practice.

You will report to the CTDO and act as a senior technology partner to business, product, change, architecture, infrastructure, information security, data, operations and third-party delivery partners. The role requires strong functional and technical leadership, and stakeholder influence across a regulated environment

The role is required to build the quality engineering practice, DevSecOps enablement, engineering standards, tooling, career frameworks and the safe adoption of AI-assisted software delivery.

Establish clear engineering accountability with you build it you run concept

new_jobs.description:
Treasury and FP&A Technology is seeking a highly accomplished and experienced Senior Engineering Manager to lead the Loan Portfolio Mitigation Application (IRIS). The successful candidate will lead a team of software developers, overseeing the design, development, and implementation of sophisticated credit risk hedge decision systems. This leadership role requires a deep understanding of financial markets, quantitative methodologies, robust software engineering principles, and proven management capabilities to drive strategic initiatives in trading, risk management, and hedging.

This is a senior technology leadership role that demands deep technical mastery, sharp business acumen, and a proven track record of architecting and delivering complex, enterprise-grade solutions at scale. The ideal candidate is a practitioner-leader who does not just direct from the sidelines, but actively engages in technical design, architectural decision-making, and hands-on development. You will serve as the definitive technology authority for IRIS, owning end-to-end solutioning from requirements through to production, while simultaneously driving multiple high-performing Agile Scrum teams with pace and precision.

A strong grounding in financial engineering
is essential — the IRIS platform is, at its core, a sophisticated financial engineering system, encompassing Credit Default Swap (CDS), Collateralized Loan Obligation (CLO), and balance sheet hedging strategies. The successful candidate will be expected to engage fluently with quantitative finance concepts, understand the mathematical and regulatory underpinnings of loan portfolio mitigation, and translate complex financial models into robust, scalable technology solutions. Your ability to communicate with clarity across both technical and non-technical audiences will be as critical as your engineering depth.

Responsibilities:

Leadership & Team Management: Lead, mentor, and manage a team of software developers, fostering a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Strategic Oversight: Define and drive the technical strategy and roadmap for software development, aligning with business objectives and market developments. Exercise strategic influence over delivery execution, resource allocation, and budget planning while ensuring predictable outcomes.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate extensively with senior traders, risk managers, product managers, and other quantitative analytics teams to understand complex business requirements and deliver innovative solutions.
Governance and Control: Work in close partnership with control functions such as Legal, Compliance, Market and Credit Risk, Audit, Finance to ensure appropriate governance and control infrastructure.
Software Engineering Excellence: Ensure the adoption of best practices in software engineering, including robust architecture, efficient coding standards, and scalable system design. Drive engineering excellence by setting expectations around clean code practices, testing strategies, design principles, and system resiliency. Champion the responsible adoption of Copilot, Devin, and other AI assisted development tools to enhance developer efficiency and experience.
System Integration & Performance: Direct the integration of quantitative libraries and models into critical front-office trading and risk management systems, ensuring high performance, reliability, and scalability.
Research & Innovation: Drive research into new quantitative techniques, market trends, regulatory changes, and application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in software engineering, ensuring the team remains at the forefront of quantitative finance.
Influence and negotiate with senior leaders across functions, as well as communicate with external parties as necessary.
Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency, as well as effectively supervise the activity of others and create accountability with those who fail to maintain these standards.

Recommended Qualifications:

Progressive experience in quantitative development or quantitative analysis within a financial institution, with a significant portion in leadership or management capacity. Strong focus on rates and credit products is essential.
Strong expertise in providing technical solutions and architectures for complex business problems, identifying the benefits and risks of the solutions, and providing customer-centric design recommendations. 5+ years of experience in senior leadership roles.
Deep, hands-on expertise in Java and the Spring Boot framework.
Expert-level proficiency in Python.
Strong understanding of RESTful API design, microservices architecture, distributed systems, and service decomposition patterns.
Strong proficiency in SQL and relational database design, with hands-on experience in Microsoft SQL Server or equivalent enterprise RDBMS.
Familiarity with financial data modelling concepts — particularly loan portfolios, balance sheet structures, credit default swaps (CDS), and regulatory reporting schemas.
Proficiency with Lightspeed pipeline frameworks or equivalent Kubernetes-native CI/CD tooling. Exposure to Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, either on premises or public clouds (e.g. Jenkins)
Strong working knowledge of OpenShift (or Kubernetes) for container orchestration, pod management, build configuration, and on-premises deployment patterns.
Experience managing Git-based SCM at an enterprise scale, including branching strategies, code review governance, and repository management.
Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop high-performing engineering teams. Experience in project management, resource allocation, and strategic planning.
Strong understanding of Agile methodologies and frameworks (e.g., Scrum, SAFe) and working in Agile teams.
Proficiency with Jira for backlog management, sprint planning, and delivery tracking at scale.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex financial challenges into robust quantitative and technical solutions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of articulating complex technical and quantitative concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior management.

Education:

Bachelors/Masters in a quantitative field such as Financial Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or equivalent.
Professional Certifications (AI, OpenShift, Agile, Architecture) – Advantageous.
Deep understanding of fixed income markets, interest rate derivatives (swaps, bonds, and loans), and interest rate curves. Extensive knowledge of credit products including Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLOs), Credit Default Swaps (CDS) and credit risk modelling (e.g., default probability and recovery rates).
Strong foundation in numerical methods and statistical analysis.
